:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
Let

$$
u=2x+1
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x} = 2 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \textrm d x=\dfrac 1 2 \, \textrm d u
$$

Before substituting, we use the table below to change the limits from $x$ to $u$.
$\begin{bmatrix}x & -2 & 1 \\ u & -3 & 3\end{bmatrix}$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\int_{-2}^{1}\sinh (2x + 1)dx &= \int_{-3}^{3}\sinh u \cdot \frac{1}{2}du \\
&= \frac{1}{2}\int_{-3}^{3}\sinh udu \\
&= \left.\frac{1}{2}\cosh u\right|_{-3}^{3} \\
&= \frac{1}{2}(\cosh 3 - \cosh (-3)) \\
&= \frac{1}{2}(\cosh 3 - \cosh 3) \\
&= 0
\end{aligned}
$$

:topic/knowledge-points.:knowledge-point/title: Integrating Hyperbolic Functions With Linear Arguments

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
Let

$$
u=3x+1
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d u}{\textrm d x} = 3\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \textrm{d}x =\dfrac{1}{3} \, \textrm{d}u
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and compute it, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\intcsch (3x + 1)\coth (3x + 1)dx &= \intcsch u\coth u \cdot \frac{1}{3}du \\
&= \frac{1}{3}\intcsch u\coth udu \\
&= \frac{1}{3}(-csch u) + C \\
&=-\frac{1}{3}csch (3x + 1) + C
\end{aligned}
$$
